# Code review: shared GS error messages (`7399f2d…HEAD`)

**Mode:** committed range, read-only. One commit, `09d2e26d2`. Merge base `4504b36` → `HEAD 09d2e26`, 9 files, +615 −58. The web, mobile and `packages/utils` areas are all touched. No on-chain code.

I didn't run tests or install anything. One side step: there's no `node_modules` in this worktree, so I checked protocol-kit's behaviour against a sibling install on this machine (8.0.7; the lockfile pins 8.0.5).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | **Fix before opening.** The new messages are never shown to anyone in production. |
| **Score** | ~74 / 100. Only the top finding was checked by a validator and a refuter; the rest are my own read at full weight. |
| **Held down by** | Bugs (F1) and testing (F2) |
| **Fix first** | F1: the only production wiring doesn't work |

## Must fix before opening

**F1 · P1 · bugs · CONFIRMED (validator 95; refuter: STANDS)**
`apps/web/src/hooks/useIsValidExecution.ts:83`: the GS → message mapping never runs for a real revert, and its result wouldn't be shown even if it did:
- **The catch never sees the promise failing.** Line 76 is `return safeContract.isValidTransaction(...)` with no `await`, so if that promise fails, the error skips the catch block.
- **The SDK never fails anyway.** protocol-kit's `isValidTransaction` wraps its own body in `try { … } catch { return false }` in every contract version.
- **The UI doesn't read `reason`.** `ExecuteForm.tsx:294-304` shows hard-coded copy, and `components/tx/ErrorMessage/index.tsx:101` shows `error.message`. Nothing renders `error.reason`.

So the new copy never reaches a user, even though the change is presented as delivering it. The missing `await` and the swallowing SDK were already there, but this PR builds its only production integration on top of them.

**Fix:** handle `isValidTransaction` returning `false`, or call the contract's own simulation directly so the revert reason comes through. Then pass the mapped message into `ErrorMessage` as its visible text instead of changing `err.reason`.

## What this review didn't cover

- **Tests weren't run**, including the snapshot test and whether the mobile Jest setup resolves the `@safe-global/utils/...` import.
- **Copy accuracy:** I didn't check each GS code's wording against the upstream Safe contract error docs beyond a spot check. The code list itself matches upstream.
- **Adjudication:** only F1 went through the paired validator and refuter. F2–F9 are single-reviewer findings.
- **Skipped steps:** the cleanup-proposal pass and "since last run" tracking, because this was a read-only review and nothing was written to `.git/`.

No findings were refuted. No tracked files were changed, and nothing was posted.
